numbering_policy: Original Saints references, chapters, reading sections, anchors and continuation bodies are preserved. Missing original verse numbers are not filled from another edition.
review_notes: Every one of Luke 1's 80 saved original source units is represented once as a paired source or a deferred source; source wording is not edited.

Internal narrative links are labeled as same-book or same-chapter connections and are not independent attestations. Similar birth settings and hymnic language do not identify distinct mothers, children or events.

Targets follow the Saints saved original numbering, including Greek-Old-Testament Psalm and Malachi divisions. Differing titles, images, audiences and narrative circumstances are retained in the rationales.

Read all 80 source units and every retained target with surrounding context; 74 distinct source units have 74 retained pairs and 6 are deferred. Original target ID existence, original-order contiguity, duplicate pairs, self-target exclusions and all-source coverage were checked.

All 52 actual Luke 2 source units and every retained target passage were read from the exact Saints cached snapshots with relevant context. Original source words, identities, display text and continuation paragraphs are unchanged.
Mark's full 673-unit source inventory had been read and the root confirmed the book boundary before this Luke source review began.

The supplied registration notices are retained without inventing a Quirinius chronology or equating unspecified censuses. Luke's Nazareth return and Matthew's Egyptian/Judean journey are compared without a merged infancy timetable.

Internal links identify precise sign/event correspondences, the repeated maternal heart-keeping formula, the parents' presentation visit and recurring infancy or response patterns. They are explicitly not independent historical attestation.

Luke's firstborn/presentation/circumcision and bird-offering references are compared with the actual Exodus and Leviticus wording. The plural their purification is not silently changed to her, and the laws are not made to require every action of every person in Luke's scene.
Isaiah's actual Greek-based sanctuary/trap wording in 8:14–15 is preserved. Salvation/light comparisons distinguish Simeon's present child testimony from Isaiah's wider restoration promises.
The sword/soul/heart-thoughts comparison with Hebrews is restricted to imagery and does not identify Mary's sword with God's word. Anna is not assigned another widow's identity or community office.

Father's house is not silently substituted for Luke2:49's what belongs to My Father. The temple-wisdom comparisons preserve child/adult ages, listening/questioning versus teaching, and distinct occasions.
Fourteen source units remain explicitly deferred with zero completion credit. Multiple targets for circumcision/naming earn only one distinct-source completion for Luke2:21.

All 38 actual Luke 3 source units and every retained target were read from exact Saints snapshots, with context. The 31 proposed completed sources have 34 distinct pairs; seven sources remain deferred with zero credit.

Target IDs resolve, original target ranges are contiguous, complete source coverage is exact, pair keys are unique, and no target contains its own source unit. No wording or continuation structure was changed.
The unique chronological list is deferred. Repeated personal names in the unmatched six lineage units do not establish identities, filiation, or connections to famous prophetic or patriarchal names.

Luke and Matthew genealogy comparisons explicitly preserve Heli versus Jacob, Neri versus Jechoniah, Rhesa versus Abiud, and Nathan versus Solomon. No maternal-line, adoption, levirate, or other historical reconciliation is invented.

Sala versus Salman, Admin and Arni versus Arran, Cainan versus Kenan, and Abram versus Abraham remain the original English forms. The documented Abram-to-Abraham name change was checked in Genesis 17:5 as broader context without rewriting Genesis 11.

Post-Flood Cainan linked to Arphaxad in Luke 3:36 and Genesis 11:12–13 is kept distinct from the pre-Flood Cainan in Luke 3:37. The original Genesis 11:13 unit already contains the Cainan-Shelah material; it was neither split into invented verse units nor replaced with a different edition's lineage.

Partial genealogy comparisons name their scope explicitly. Samuel establishes Nathan among David's sons but does not confirm Melea, Menna, or Mattatha; Chronicles 1:3–4 supports Lamech-Noah-Shem without silently adding Cainan.

John's audience differs between Luke's crowds and Matthew's Pharisees and Sadducees. Fire in Luke's Spirit baptism and bodily form/upon Him in the baptism scene are not inserted into Mark's actual supplied wording.

Ethical parallels specify their scope: food and clothing; tax-collection extortion and restitution; or monetary contentment. Hebrews is not represented as repeating every command directed to soldiers.

Read all 182 actual saved source units: Luke4 has44, Luke5 has39, Luke6 has49, Luke7 has50. Every retained target and relevant surrounding context was read from exact Saints originals; source wording, display text, numbering and continuation units are unchanged.

172 distinct source units have175 retained pairs;10 source units remain deferred with zero completion credit. Extra pairs cover separate useful clauses at4:18 and6:21 and the Gospel/prophetic counterparts at7:27.

The temptation order and stone/stones difference, Isaiah's actual release wording, the shortened acceptable-year reading, and Psalms90 numbering are retained. Deuteronomy's fear/serve formulation is distinguished from Luke's worship/serve answer.

Luke's Judea at4:44 is preserved alongside Mark's Galilee. Hometown visits, boat teaching, distinct fish catches, varied healings and different raising events are compared without a merged itinerary or chronology.
Levi is not assigned another tax collector's identity; Judas of James is not equated with a differently named apostle. The apostle-list sequence and titles remain those of each saved account.

Blessings and woes retain poor versus poor in spirit, hunger versus righteousness, laughter versus comfort, merciful versus perfect, and the distinct temporal or group contrasts. Clause-level support is explicit where another account does not reproduce an entire verse.

The centurion's elders and friends are not inserted into Matthew's directly narrated appeal. Luke's unnamed anointing woman is not identified as Mary or assigned another woman's history; different meals, tears, perfume, gestures and speakers remain distinguished.

Internal links identify contrasting assessments or parable/application and repeated teaching patterns; they are not independent witnesses. Debt forgiveness and love retain Luke's supplied wording without adding a causal theory of earned forgiveness.
Target ID existence, original-order contiguous ranges, duplicate pairs, no self-targets and complete paired/deferred source coverage were verified.

All 214 actual source units in Luke 8–11, including every unique narrative or parable detail, were read from the exact cached Saints originals. Every retained target was read with relevant context. Original text, unit IDs, numbering gaps and continuation paragraphs remain unchanged.

Proposals prioritize the close Markan and Matthean accounts while explicitly preserving different audience descriptions, details, sequence notices and additions. Related passages do not establish that every clause of a source unit is independently attested.

Mark 16:9 is used only for Mary Magdalene's seven-demon identification, with its double-bracketed longer-ending status explicit. Luke's named women and their belongings are not silently equated with all of Mark's named women.

The Gerasene texts preserve the actual supplied locality name. Abyss is not replaced with country, lake with sea, or a city proclamation with Decapolis. The Jairus narrative remains about a dying daughter at the initial request rather than borrowing Matthew's different initial timing.

The travel instructions preserve Luke and Matthew's staff restriction and do not rewrite Mark's permission. The Twelve and the seventy-two are distinct stated missions, including where an internal advance-messenger pattern is compared.

Transfiguration comparisons preserve about eight days versus six days, chosen versus beloved, the actual prayer/sleep details, and the differing secrecy formulations. No chronological reconciliation is invented.

Internal and thematic links are labeled. The approaching taking-up notice is compared with Luke's eventual ascent without relocating Bethany or the ascent date to the start of the Jerusalem journey. Prophetic departure dialogue is compared with later Jerusalem-fulfillment teaching within explicit limits.

The Samaritan rejection and John's Samaritan conversation have distinct villagers and outcomes; Jerusalem supplies a limited setting comparison. The fire proposal recalls Elijah's fire without inserting Elijah's name into Luke's supplied sentence or erasing Jesus' rebuke.

Isaiah 14's fall-from-heaven imagery is compared only as imagery: its stated Babylonian-king context is not converted into a historical identity with Satan. Psalm 90 retains this canon's actual asp, basilisk, lion and dragon wording and numbering.

The good-neighbor story's unique victim, priest, Levite and inn-payment details are deferred. Internal interpretation links identify the story's own mercy/action conclusion and changed neighbor-question framing. The Chronicles comparison concerns bounded care, transport and Jericho motifs, not identical victims or an independent Samaritan biography.

Mary's listening at Jesus' feet is compared with Paul's feet-of-a-teacher education description without assigning her his formal institution or curriculum. Martha's hospitality and service do not make the two Gospel meals the same visit or fix Luke's unnamed village as Bethany.

Luke's shorter prayer is retained as supplied. Our, in the heavens, God's-will and deliverance-from-evil petitions are not inserted from Matthew. Sins/debts, Holy Spirit/good things, and egg-scorpion/bread-stone examples remain distinct.

The friend and widow comparison supports the response-to-insistence teaching, with different requests and motives and no simple equation of God to the unwilling human characters. The midnight setup's unique details are deferred rather than multiplied into generic hospitality links.

The cup controversy distinguishes Jesus from the disciples questioned in Mark. Unmarked versus whitewashed tombs, knowledge-key versus kingdom-door imagery, Luke's herbs and virtues, and the different tomb-builders' claims are explicitly distinguished.

Zechariah's unnamed father in Luke is not supplied from Matthew or identified with a different historical person. Divine Wisdom's prophets/apostles and Jesus' prophets/wise people/scribes are preserved in their actual forms.
Completed distinct-source counts are separate from pair totals. The love-command unit has two scriptural targets but earns one source completion. Deferred units earn zero credit.

All 192 actual Luke 12–16 source units and all retained targets were read from the exact Saints snapshots with context. The proposed 162 paired sources have 162 distinct pairs; 30 sources remain deferred with zero completion credit.

Every relationship has an individual explanation. Distinct settings, speakers, roles, monetary details, images, and differing narrated versus alleged actions remain explicit. The initial pass is selective rather than an exhaustive concordance.

Same-book links explicitly identify recurring teaching, parable motifs, mirrored speeches, planned-and-reported fulfillment, and deliberate refrains. They do not provide independent witnesses or turn adjacent accounts into the same event.

Sirach 11:18–19 is compared with the rich-fool story's wealth, rest, enjoyment, uncertain lifespan, and goods left to others; it does not supply Luke's agricultural yield, storehouse demolition, or this-night timing.

The Sabbath ruler's six-working-days argument is compared with Exodus without making Exodus explicitly forbid healing. Other Sabbath controversies retain different patients, actions, examples, and response sequences.

Proverbs comparisons use the actual Saints wording, including 24:6's steering and deliberative heart and 24:27's field preparation and rebuilding. Neither passage is silently rewritten with a familiar alternative edition's wording.

Banquet parallels preserve king versus ordinary householder, wedding versus supper, servants' numbers, named versus unspecified excuses, guest categories, and differing invitation words. The new-marriage duty exemption does not establish a legal exemption from the parable's feast.

The return of the younger son preserves narration versus the older brother's allegation about prostitutes. No cause is invented for omission of the planned hired-worker request from the recorded confession. Dead/alive restoration language is not automatically made a literal bodily resurrection.

The steward is accused of scattering another's possessions; the son is narrated scattering his own. The master's commendation is expressly about prudence and does not erase the description unrighteous or endorse dishonest transactions.

No speculative interest-rate, commission, inheritance-share, or historical-family theory is used to explain unique figures or people. Unknown five brothers are not identified with an actual family or a symbolic set.

Luke's parable Lazarus and John's Bethany Lazarus remain distinct figures. John's resurrection and mixed responses are compared with the parable's proposed miracle argument without inferring identity from a repeated name.
Hades, Abraham's bosom, kingdom exclusion, and other judgment images retain their wording and settings. The record adds no afterlife geography or identification of the fixed chasm with another place.
